Taken up by the subscriber at Prairie du Chien, Michigan Territory, about two miles and a half from the fort, on the 6th day of August last, a HORSE, described as follows, to wit:—“A bright brown horse 6 years old past, fifteen and a half hands high, both right feet white, a pale star on his forehead, and snip on his nose, a small dent in the left side of his neck, black switch tail and mane, and paces.” The above horse I am desirous the rightful owner should have. I have advertised him in several places, and now in the paper, thinking by this means the proper owner will be better able to find his lost horse. The horse is in my possession, near Carlyle, Clinton county, Illinois, and will be kept for the owner, and delivered up on proof, and payment of the charges of the advertisements. REUBEN T. HAWKINS. Carlyle, Sept. 1, 1837. U. S. Mail Stage. The subscriber has commenced running a line of four-horse coaches from Vandalia to Macoupin Point, twice a week. Travelers from the east for Springfield and the northern parts of the State, will find this one of the most convenient and expeditious routes. This line intersects the line of stages from Springfield to St. Louis twice a week, at Macoupin Point, and the line from Mmsville to St. Louis once a week, at Vandalia.

HAVING now received the largest stock of Goods for the season, we are determined to offer greater inducements to the country trade than ever before, as we are prepared to offer goods from our own importation, and from large purchases in the Eastern markets, for proof of which we respectfully solicit an inspection of our stock and prices. All competitors must be the actual owners of the animals entered by them, on the first day of July 1855, and such ownership must have continued to the day of the Show. Security will be required that every Bull, to which a premium is awarded, shall be kept within the State for twelve months succeeding the Show. No animal will be allowed to enter into competition in more than one class. All animals offered for competition must be entered with William A. Lincoln, the Secretary of this Committee, in Worcester, on or before WEDNESDAY, the 26th day of SEPTEMBER, at 12 o’clock, noon, and must be exhibited upon the grounds of the Worcester Agricultural Society, on the day of exhibition, at 8 A. M., and remain till 3 P. M. TRAVEL. The Trustees will pay at the rate of 12 cents per mile to the owners of such animals as obtain premiums and which are brought or driven more than 10 miles from the place of exhibiting, computing from the place from which the animals come; unsuccessful competitors the like sum if upon the report of any committee such an indemnity for expense should be merited.

The undersigned having purchased the well-known corner, on Walnut and Farmer streets, formerly occupied by Mr. Alfred Clark, and erected a large and commodious Stable, would respectfully inform the citizens of this and the adjoining counties, and the public generally, that he will at all times, keep fine saddle & Harness Horses, for Sale or Hire; also, fine Buggies and Hacks. From his well-known reputation as a Livery Stable keeper, he hopes to receive a generous patronage. The following are his rates for Horse Hire, Feed, &c. Hire of Hack per day, $5 00; Horse and Buggy per day, $4 00; Saddle Horse, $2 50; Harness Horse, $1 25; Buggy and Harness, $1 50; Feed per Month, $12 00; Week, $4 00; Single Feed, $0 25. All losses or injury done to horses or rigging, must be accounted for at a fair estimate. All travelers wishing private conveyance, by calling at his stable, can obtain any mode of travel they may desire. His horses being well and gently trained, there will be no danger of breakage or loss of life. Fine Horses, Mules and Scrubs, on hand and for sale. He will give a good washing, rubbing, carding, currying and a full feed, all for Forty Cents. From an arrangement he has made with an experienced Horse Trader, he is enabled to furnish, at short notice, Pairs, or any kind of horses which may be wanted.
